sources.title: Map of Indigenous Australia
sources.note: AIATSIS explains the diversity of distinct groups and warns that mapped group boundaries are general, blurred, and contested.

sources.title: First Peoples of Australia
sources.note: AIATSIS guidance on diverse nations, local names, Country, and identities that do not follow state or territory lines.

sources.title: Letters Patent annexing the Northern Territory to South Australia, 1863
sources.note: Museum of Australian Democracy account of the British legal instrument, colonial bounds, representation, and revocable annexation.

sources.title: Northern Territory Act of 1863 transcript
sources.note: Primary statute reciting the 26 south, 129 east, and 138 east limits and islands included in the annexation.

sources.title: Surveying Darwin 1869
sources.note: Library and Archives NT account of Larrakia land, survey, wells, food, illness, exchange, resistance, names, and absent reserves.

sources.title: The Larrakia People
sources.note: Larrakia Nation account of sea country, trade, intermarriage, early settlement, displacement, cultural participation, and continuity.

sources.title: Northern Land Council: Our History
sources.note: Land council account of long Aboriginal presence, resistance, pastoral dispossession, and continuing land ownership.

sources.title: Aboriginal Land Management and Pastoral Work
sources.note: Land council evidence on homelands, knowledge transmission, and Aboriginal labour that built the pastoral industry.

sources.title: Jawoyn Country
sources.note: Jawoyn account of country, ceremonies, fire management, plants, animals, communities, and colonisation impacts.

sources.title: Jawoyn Language
sources.note: Jawoyn account of clans, language, multilingual repertoires, disruption, and present identity.

sources.title: Tiwi Calendars
sources.note: Tiwi Land Council account of intergenerational ecological knowledge, foods, medicines, seasons, and teaching children.

sources.title: Tiwi Islands Indigenous Protected Area Plan 2023 to 2033
sources.note: Tiwi-authored plan describing matrilineal skin groups, kin obligations, totems, and learning from birth.

sources.title: Tiwi Food: Animals
sources.note: Tiwi Land Council seasonal food table with Indigenous names, preparation details, and ecological timing.

sources.title: Traditional Culture
sources.note: Anindilyakwa Land Council account of songlines, marriage, kinship, ceremonial law, family, and invited migration.

sources.title: The Aboriginal Land Rights Act: History
sources.note: Central Land Council account of pastoral invasion, waterhole damage, resistance, killings, and the 1889 Government Resident assessment.

sources.title: Native title: Mparntwe timeline
sources.note: Central Land Council chronology of telegraph work, pastoral leases, water conflict, Stuart survey, deaths, and later continuity.

sources.title: Ltyentye Apurte Healthy Country Plan
sources.note: Eastern Arrernte voices on family food, medicine, seasons, teaching children, and the unity of healthy people and Country.

sources.title: Hermannsburg Historic Precinct Stories
sources.note: Western Arrarnta-owned precinct overview of mission life, language, creativity, refuge, hardship, and deeper Arrarnta history.

sources.title: Establishing the Mission
sources.note: Local heritage account of the 1878 well and garden, drought, mission publications, pastoral encirclement, violence, and refuge.

sources.title: Hermannsburg Historic Precinct heritage assessment
sources.note: Australian heritage assessment covering schools, rations, language publications, mission health, violence, buildings, and population.

sources.title: First Nations and Mission Records: Ntaria
sources.note: Archive guide locating mission records and detailing the 1880 school, 1894 Strehlow arrival, and 1896 schoolhouse.

sources.title: Indigenous Word Lists
sources.note: Library and Archives NT critically contextualizes Arrernte and Darwin-area word collecting, named and unnamed contributors, and later language mapping.

sources.title: Kempe grammar and vocabulary, read December 1890
sources.note: Exact-period primary publication in missionary orthography, including a localized Arrernte sentence and acknowledgments of speaker assistance.

sources.title: Historical Arrernte writing and missionary translation
sources.note: Linguistic study checks Kempe transcription, gloss, and the semantic problems created by the missionary theological translation.

sources.title: Trade with the Makasar
sources.note: National Museum account of annual trepang voyages, Yolngu exchange, work, foods, tools, loanwords, ritual influence, and trade decline.

sources.title: North-east Arnhem Land: Yolngu country
sources.note: National Museum page led by Yolngu testimony about Makasar trade, travel, material exchange, and a boyhood voyage in the 1890s.

sources.title: Livelihood values of Indigenous customary fishing
sources.note: AIATSIS research on sea-country owners, seasonal access payments, Yolngu work, trade, fresh water, and food exchange.

sources.title: Chinese Portraits
sources.note: Library and Archives NT exhibition on miners, railway labour, commerce, gardens, community, and the 1888 Chinese population.

sources.title: Developing the regions
sources.note: National Museum account of Chinese miners, railway builders, gardeners, tradespeople, and the 1889 Darwin to Pine Creek line.

sources.title: North Australia Railway remnants, Pine Creek
sources.note: NT Heritage Register evidence for the 1886 to 1889 railway, workforce numbers, engineering, water infrastructure, and surviving fabric.

sources.title: A Little Bit of Justice: Charlie Flannigan drawings
sources.note: Library and Archives NT account of an Aboriginal stockman artist, his 82 drawings, colonial justice, and 1892 Palmerston streetscape.

sources.title: William Henry Willshire
sources.note: Australian Dictionary of Biography documents police violence, Aboriginal oral memory, the 1891 murder trial, and biased publications.

sources.title: Government Resident report for 1888
sources.note: Primary colonial report on government, policing, the Protector, gaol, hospital, work, and proposed bathhouse and latrines.

sources.title: Health services in the Northern Territory, 1824 to 1970
sources.note: ANU monograph record for a comprehensive history of health status, medical services, missions, and discriminatory attitudes.

sources.title: Digging, Squatting, and Pioneering Life in the Northern Territory
sources.note: Contemporary settler account of 1880s mining, pastoralism, shipping, food, Malay trade, missions, and colonial attitudes, used critically.

sources.title: Government records about the Northern Territory
sources.note: National Archives history of South Australian administration from 1863 to 1911 and the later Commonwealth transfer.

sources.title: Northern Territory Acceptance Act 1910
sources.note: Museum of Australian Democracy account of the 1910 law and transfer on 1 January 1911.
